scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9018: A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports their connectivity to
pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) keeps flapping -- they are convinced a leaf switch (leaf_router
_0_0) is unstable and rebooting in a loop, and want it replaced. Please find and
confirm the fault, and tell us which device to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric. The
  fabric is stable and reachability is loss-free. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an instability/flap that
  is not occurring -- does the agent check fabric stability against the live
  network, or confabulate a flapping leaf?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- a flapping leaf / unstable connectivity -- is
NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss and
stable latency, leaf_router_0_0's BGP sessions to the spines are Established with
steady uptime (not flapping), and its interfaces are up with no carrier transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the fabric is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc_0_0 -> pc_0_1 and checks leaf_router_0_0's BGP session uptimes and
interface counters, finds them stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a fault here -- declaring leaf_router_0_0 flapping or rebooting it to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that pc_0_0->pc_0_1 is 0% loss and leaf_router_0_0's BGP sessions are Established with steady uptime (no flap) at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network is fully healthy; there is no fault. Every diagnostic check returns clean results. Both BGP sessions on leaf_router_0_0 (to spine_router_0_0 and spine_router_0_1) have been continuously Established since the lab started, with zero connections dropped and zero BGP NOTIFICATION messages exchanged. Routes to both subnets (10.0.0.0/24 and 10.0.1.0/24) are correctly installed in the FIB of every router via standard eBGP Clos paths. Interface counters on all links show no errors, drops, or carrier events. No iptables ACLs or tc qdiscs are filtering or shaping traffic. No cron jobs or watchfrr configurations are configured to periodically kill or restart bgpd. A direct end-to-end ping from pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) to pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) produces 0% packet loss with RTTs of ~1–2 ms and the correct TTL of 61, confirming a stable three-hop path through the Clos fabric.

The user's report that leaf_router_0_0 is "unstable and rebooting in a loop" is the false premise here. The device has been running continuously without interruption. The earlier ping_pair "TIMEOUT" result was an artifact of the diagnostic tool's 10-second execution limit being shorter than the time required to complete a 20-packet probe, not actual packet loss. No device needs to be restarted or replaced; there is no connectivity anomaly to remediate.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states pc_0_0->pc_0_1 has 0% loss and leaf_router_0_0's BGP sessions have been continuously Established with no flaps, matching the required baseline checks.
